Maintenance Report — MNT-0100-001

Asset: WELL-0100 (SW-24 Well 100, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: wellhead Work started: 02 Dec 2022 08:00 · Finished: 06 Dec 2022 23:00 · Well stopped for this job: 111 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0100-0007 on 2022-12-01 Report written: 06 Dec 2022

What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw a thin film of oil on the wellhead. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0100-0007 showed the wellhead at 7.9 °C with the air at 8.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The packing rings were worn and the polished rod was lightly scored. The well stayed shut in for about 3 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

Packing wear sped up by a slightly misaligned polished rod.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Closed the wellhead valves and bled off pressure.
  2. Removed the old packing.
  3. Installed new packing rings and adjusted the gland.
  4. Cleaned the wellhead area.

Summary of the fix: replaced stuffing box packing.

Testing and return to service

Checked the stuffing box with the unit running: no leak. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0100-005

Asset: WELL-0100 (SW-24 Well 100, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 29 Apr 2023 08:00 · Finished: 03 May 2023 16:00 · Well stopped for this job: 104 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0100-0028 on 2023-04-27 Report written: 04 May 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0100-0028 showed the wellhead at 29.7 °C with the air at 24.2 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 2 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

Safety and permits

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0100-009

Asset: WELL-0100 (SW-24 Well 100, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 12 Jan 2024 08:00 · Finished: 16 Jan 2024 02:00 · Well stopped for this job: 90 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0100-0059 on 2024-01-11 Report written: 17 Jan 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0100-0059 showed the wellhead at 10.2 °C with the air at 6.2 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 2 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 5 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0100-015

Asset: WELL-0100 (SW-24 Well 100, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 28 Jun 2024 08:00 · Finished: 28 Jun 2024 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 10 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0100-0083 on 2024-06-27 Report written: 30 Jun 2024

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0100-0083 at 13:30 on 2024-06-27 found crude oil on the pad: about 7.4% of the pad area, estimated 3.3 bbl. The inspector noted: "Staining along flowline route." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 4.5 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a corrosion hole along the flowline route.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak point.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in new line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 252 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 202 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 2.6 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0100-015 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.37% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0100-034

Asset: WELL-0100 (SW-24 Well 100, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 11 Sep 2026 08:00 · Finished: 11 Sep 2026 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 10 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0100-0196 on 2026-09-10 Report written: 12 Sep 2026

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0100-0196 at 10:00 on 2026-09-10 found crude oil on the pad: about 1.0% of the pad area, estimated 0.4 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 8.1 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

Root cause

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 8 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Cleaned free oil out of the cellar.
  2. Unbolted the flange and removed the failed gasket.
  3. Fitted a new gasket and new bolts, torqued to specification.
  4. Excavated the stained soil around the cellar.

Summary of the fix: replaced the flange gasket and bolts and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 252 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 202 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 0.5 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0100-034 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.48% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).
